title: What a pharmacy licence renewal requires, and non-transferability
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 6.04(8) a pharmacy license shall be non-transferrable. Under 247 CMR 6.04(9), which governs renewal of Drug Store Pharmacy, sterile compounding, complex non-sterile compounding, institutional sterile compounding, non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy, non-resident sterile compounding and non-resident complex non-sterile compounding pharmacy licenses and controlled substance registrations: application for renewal of a pharmacy license and controlled substance registration shall be made by a duly authorized representative of the pharmacy in the form and manner determined by the Board, and the renewal form shall be fully and properly completed and submitted in a timely manner; the licensee shall submit payment of a non-refundable licensing and application fee as determined by the Executive Office of Administration and Finance; each renewal application shall be accompanied by an attestation that the pharmacy complied with all mandatory reporting during that licensing period in accordance with 247 CMR 20.00; and the Board may renew a pharmacy license and controlled substance registration if it finds, in its reasonable discretion, that the licensee and any interest holder are suitable and approving the application would be consistent with the best interest of public health, welfare and safety. Under 247 CMR 6.18 no pharmacy shall be denied initial licensure or denied renewal due to any complaint, criminal charge, conviction, judgment, discipline or other sanction due to providing or assisting in providing, or dispensing medication for, reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services as defined at M.G.L. c. 12, s. 11I1/2, so long as the services would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with standards for good professional practice in Massachusetts.
exam_relevance: Tests that renewal is a discretionary Board decision resting on suitability and a reporting attestation, not an automatic fee payment, and that a pharmacy licence cannot be transferred.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

exceptions: 247 CMR 6.18 bars denial of initial licensure or renewal on the listed grounds arising from legally protected reproductive or gender-affirming health care that would have been lawful in Massachusetts and is consistent with good professional practice there.
common_confusions: Renewal is not automatic on payment: the Board may renew if it finds the licensee and any interest holder suitable.
The attestation covers compliance with all mandatory reporting under 247 CMR 20.00 during the licensing period.
247 CMR 6.00 states no grace period, late-renewal procedure or reinstatement procedure for a pharmacy licence.
verification_notes: Read in the Board's publication of 247 CMR 6.00 (PDF) on mass.gov on 2026-09-17.
